idea: Implement the strip-mixing form directly. Use x rows of a squares of side 1/a and y rows of a+1 squares of side 1/(a+1), with x/a + y/(a+1) ≤ 1, then put a final leftover row of c squares in the residual height. Enumerate a, x, y and c, which naturally yields values like (k·j + b)/j that match the best-known pattern for even n.
